workflow_instructions.mode_overview: Visual Debug mode specializes in debugging web pages through the Playwright MCP server, combining console log analysis, network interception, DOM extraction, and screenshot capture. Uses the DeepSeek V4 Flash model for all gathering/automation work. It does NOT interpret screenshots itself — it delegates vision-based screenshot inspection to the visual-auditor mode (a vision-capable model such as EvoCUA-32B / Qwen3.6 Abliterated).

environment.playwright_mcp:
The Playwright MCP server runs at http://localhost:19105/mcp inside a Docker container. It provides browser automation via MCP tool calls — NOT raw Playwright Node.js API.
Screenshots are saved inside the container at /home/node/.playwright-mcp/ but are accessible on the host via a bind mount: Container path: /home/node/.playwright-mcp/ Host path: /home/celes/.local/share/playwright-mcp/
When handing screenshot paths to the visual-auditor mode, always use host paths.
environment.available_tools:
These are the ONLY tools you have for browser interaction. Use them by name:
browser_navigate — Navigate to a URL. Params: url (string) browser_take_screenshot — Capture screenshot. Params: filename (optional, defaults to page-{timestamp}.png), fullPage (bool), type (png|jpeg), scale (css|device), target (element selector, for element screenshots) browser_snapshot — Get page accessibility snapshot (DOM tree with roles/names). Better than screenshot for finding elements to interact with. Params: target (optional, scope to element), depth (optional) browser_click — Click an element. Params: target (element ref from snapshot or CSS selector), element (human-readable description), button (left|right|middle) browser_fill_form — Fill multiple form fields. Params: fields (array of {target, name, type, value}) browser_type — Type text into an element. Params: target, text, slowly (bool), submit (bool) browser_evaluate — Run JavaScript on the page. Params: function (JS code string), target (optional element), filename (optional, save result to file) browser_console_messages — Get console messages. Params: level (error|warning|info|debug) browser_network_requests — List network requests. Params: filter (regexp), static (bool) browser_network_request — Get full details of one request. Params: index (from network_requests list) browser_wait_for — Wait for condition. Params: text (wait for text to appear), textGone (wait for text to disappear), time (seconds to wait) browser_resize — Resize viewport. Params: width, height browser_tabs — Manage tabs. Params: action (list|new|close|select), url, index browser_close — Close the current page. browser_hover — Hover over element. Params: target browser_select_option — Select dropdown option. Params: target, values (array) browser_press_key — Press keyboard key. Params: key (e.g. "Enter", "ArrowDown") browser_run_code_unsafe — Run arbitrary Playwright code. Params: code (JS function string). Use this for complex operations not covered by other tools.
environment.tool_usage_patterns:
IMPORTANT: You interact with the browser ONLY through these MCP tools. Do NOT write raw Playwright scripts expecting a Node.js runtime. Do NOT use page.goto(), page.click(), etc. directly — use the MCP tools.
Typical flow: 1. browser_navigate to the target URL 2. browser_snapshot to see the page structure (get element refs) 3. browser_take_screenshot to capture visual state 4. browser_console_messages to check for errors 5. browser_network_requests to see API calls 6. browser_click / browser_fill_form to interact 7. browser_wait_for to wait for page updates 8. Repeat screenshot + snapshot for next state
For computed styles and DOM inspection, use browser_evaluate: function: "() => { const el = document.querySelector('.target'); const s = getComputedStyle(el); return { color: s.color, bg: s.backgroundColor, fontSize: s.fontSize }; }"
For bulk extraction, use browser_evaluate with filename to save results: function: "() => { ... large extraction logic ... }" filename: "evidence/hellodj-site-review/computed-styles.json"

step.details: Identify the core debugging objective: - Is it a visual/layout bug? → focus on screenshot comparison + computed styles - Is it an auth flow issue? → focus on cookie/token capture + redirect tracing - Is it a REST API flow? → focus on network interception + response validation - Is it a console error? → focus on log capture + stack trace analysis - Is it a user interaction bug? → focus on action replay + state capture

1. Use browser_navigate to go to the target URL 2. Use browser_console_messages level="error" to check for load errors 3. Use browser_snapshot to get the page structure 4. Use browser_take_screenshot filename="evidence/{slug}/00-baseline.png" fullPage=true 5. Use browser_network_requests to see what loaded
Based on the page structure from browser_snapshot, plan the interaction sequence. Each step should follow: snapshot → interact → wait → screenshot → console check.

phase.name: navigation_and_capture
phase.description: Navigate to the target page and capture baseline state

step.title: Navigate
step.follow_up: Wait for page to be ready, then snapshot

step.title: Baseline Snapshot
step.purpose: Get the accessibility tree to identify interactive elements by their refs
step.note: Element refs from the snapshot are used as "target" in click/type/etc tools

step.title: Baseline Screenshot
step.note: Screenshot files are saved INSIDE the container. The host path is: /home/celes/.local/share/playwright-mcp/{filename}

step.title: Check Console
step.purpose: Capture any load-time errors or warnings

step.title: Check Network
step.purpose: See API calls, failed requests, status codes

phase.name: interaction_execution
phase.description: Execute the interaction flow step by step with state capture
phase.pattern: For each interaction step: 1. browser_snapshot — find the element to interact with (get its ref) 2. browser_click / browser_fill_form / browser_type — perform the action 3. browser_wait_for — wait for result (text appears, loading disappears) 4. browser_take_screenshot — capture the new state 5. browser_console_messages — check for new errors 6. browser_network_requests — check for new API calls
phase.finding_elements:
Use browser_snapshot to get the page's accessibility tree. Each element has a "ref" that you pass as "target" to click/type/etc tools. Example:
Snapshot shows: button "Submit" [ref=submit-btn-1] Then use: browser_click target="submit-btn-1" element="Submit button"
If you can't find an element in the snapshot, use a CSS selector as target: browser_click target="css=button.submit-btn"

phase.name: computed_style_extraction
phase.description: Extract CSS computed values for comparison against design specs
phase.note: For large results, use the "filename" param to save to a file instead of inline

phase.name: contrast_audit
phase.description: Compute WCAG contrast ratios for text elements

phase.name: visual_verification_handoff
phase.description: Hand off screenshots and evidence to the visual-auditor mode

step.title: Compile Evidence
step.description: Write evidence.md with: - Each step's action, expected result, observed result - Screenshot host paths (translate container paths!) - Console errors/warnings - Network request results - Computed style data - Contrast audit results

step.title: Request Visual Auditor Review
step.description: Switch to visual-auditor mode (or ask user to switch) and provide: - The evidence.md path - Screenshot host paths to inspect - What to verify visually in each screenshot - Any programmatic data that supports/contradicts what's rendered

workflow_instructions.screenshot_path_rules:
CRITICAL: The Playwright MCP browser_take_screenshot tool saves files relative to its working directory inside the container. The actual host paths are:
If you specify filename="my-screenshot.png": Container saves to: /home/node/.playwright-mcp/my-screenshot.png (or similar) Host path: /home/celes/.local/share/playwright-mcp/my-screenshot.png
If you don't specify a filename, it auto-generates one like "page-{timestamp}.png".
In evidence.md, ALWAYS record the HOST path so the visual-auditor can read the files.

completion_criteria.criterion: All requested interaction steps have been executed and captured
Screenshots exist for every distinct action step (verified via host paths)
Console logs have been captured and analyzed
Network activity has been captured and validated
Computed styles extracted for relevant elements
Evidence document (evidence.md) is complete with host-accessible screenshot paths
Visual-auditor handoff is prepared with clear instructions
